guide: Open Start and type your business name, your utilisation levels, your depreciation setting, the discount for an idle gap and the profit you want from one vehicle a month.
Check Vehicles, Vehicle classes, Rate card and Seasons: they hold the fleet, the day prices and the season multipliers every other sheet reads.
Fill Vehicle months once a month: available and rented days, revenue and each cost line for every vehicle. Utilisation, idle days and profit fill in.
Read Utilisation by vehicle and Utilisation by class and month to see the red, amber and green vehicles against your own last 3 months and last year.
Open Profit per vehicle, Break-even by vehicle and Vehicle verdict list to see which cars earn their place and which are a reprice or a sell.
Record idle runs of 3 or more days in Idle runs; the lost revenue, the offer price and the revenue if the run is filled fill in.
Keep Bookings and ADR by class and month up to date to see the achieved rate, the discount share and the rate against last year.
Type the week, fleet days and booked days in Demand forecast 12 weeks to see shortage and surplus days and the weekend load.
Use the 18 tools for the weekly questions: which car to offer, how low a price can go, which vehicle to sell, whether the fleet fits.
Read Month trend and the Monthly Performance Review for the month against your last 3 months and last year.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Profit and Utilisation Dashboard and the Charts every week.
A one-car host can use the same sheets with one vehicle and one channel: the break-even and the verdict tell whether the car pays.

listing.title: Car Rental Utilisation, Profit and Pricing Review Excel Template: Profit per Vehicle, Break-even, Idle Days, ADR, Forecast
listing.headline: See which cars earn their place, where the idle days are and what to charge
listing.description:
Run the numbers side of a small car and van rental or a car-sharing host fleet in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-operator and a manager who need to know whether each car earns its place: utilisation (rented days as a share of available days) by vehicle and class with red, amber and green bands from your own settings, profit per vehicle per available day, break-even utilisation per vehicle and a keep, reprice or sell verdict. Vehicle months holds revenue and every cost line (financing, insurance, maintenance, cleaning, fuel or charge, depreciation and marketplace fees) for each vehicle and month; Profit per vehicle, Break-even by vehicle and Cost per day by vehicle fill in by themselves. Profit here is a contribution before office pay and overhead.

Idle runs lists runs of idle days with the revenue lost at the class rate, an offer price and the revenue if filled. ADR by class and month and ADR against last year show the achieved average daily rate (revenue per rented day) against the rate card, the discount share and the same month last year. Demand forecast 12 weeks sets booked days against fleet days with Base, Best and Worst scenarios and the weekend load. Month trend, Channel profit and RevPAC by class (revenue per available car-day) complete the picture.

18 decision tools answer the weekly questions: which car to offer for an idle gap, how low a price can go, which vehicle loses money, whether the fleet is the right size, which class needs how much utilisation and how this month compares with your last 3 months. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to the owner, the manager, renters, corporate accounts, a hotel partner, marketplace support, the accountant, the lender and the mechanic.

This is part seven of the Car Rental Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Renters appear by first name and initial only. Miles are the demo unit, set your own; every target is an example, set your own. It helps you keep track of your numbers and does not promise results; confirm tax questions with your adviser.
